The statement’s 25 bp cut to 4.25–4.50% alongside “roughly balanced” risks and continued balance‑sheet runoff signals cautious easing consistent with rule‑like, gradual policy in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler’s framework and forecast‑based flexible inflation targeting in Svensson and Woodford (2005). The acknowledgment that labor markets have “eased” while unemployment “has moved up but remains low” is consistent with Okun’s law and a New Keynesian Phillips Curve mechanism in which softer labor conditions reduce real marginal cost and inflation pressure. Operationally, the reduction in interest on reserve balances and use of standing facilities aligns with Goodfriend (2002) on corridor/floor systems, while maintaining ON RRP at the range floor and ongoing QT keeps financial conditions from turning outright accommodative. The lone dissent to hold rates underscores inflation‑persistence and time‑inconsistency concerns (inflation bias), tempering the dovish read. Net tone: cautiously positive for activity, with vigilance on inflation.
